unit: Students can describe their daily study routines, discuss learning tools, and share advice for building good study habits while balancing school and family life.
objective: Identify common study distractions and give advice on how to avoid them.

title: Warm-up
subtitle: Let's talk about studying.
question: How do you stay focused when your house is noisy or the TV is on?
starters: When the TV is on, I usually...
To stay focused in a noisy house, I...

title: Useful Language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat it.
Read the definition and the example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: to stop a machine, light, or phone from working
words.example: I turn off my phone when I'm studying.
words.check: When you go to sleep, do you turn off the lights or leave them on?

words.definition: to give all your attention to one thing
words.example: It's hard to focus when the house is noisy.
words.check: Is it easier to focus in a quiet room or a noisy room?

title: Useful Language (Part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat.
Read the definition and example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: An electronic game played on a computer, phone, or TV.
words.example: I want to play a video game, but I have to finish my homework first.
words.check: Which is a video game: Super Mario or playing football outside?

words.definition: A message or alert on your phone that tells you something new.
words.example: I get a loud notification on my phone when my mom sends me a message.
words.check: Do you get notifications from a paper book or a smartphone?

words.definition: The flat surface of a TV, phone, or computer that shows pictures and words.
words.example: Looking at a phone screen for too long can make your eyes tired.
words.check: Which item has a screen: a laptop or a paper notebook?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to give advice about staying focused.

linkers.use: To say what is good to do.
To say what is bad to do.

model:
A: I can't focus at all. Someone is playing a really loud video game.
B: Well, you shouldn't sit near the screen. It's a good idea to find a quiet room.

your_turn.teacher: Pretend you are distracted. Read the tutor's line and have the student give you advice.
your_turn.student:
Tutor: My phone is getting so many notifications. I just can't finish my homework!
Student: (Give advice. Use: You should... / You shouldn't... / It's a good idea to... / turn off)

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine I'm trying to study, but my family is watching TV really loudly. On top of that, my phone keeps getting a lot of notifications. What should I do? Give me some advice using the phrases below.
student_guide: You should ___ so you can focus.

title: Real-world scenario
role_a: Helpful friend: You want to help your friend study.
role_b: Distracted student: You can't finish your homework because you keep playing a video game.
problem: Your friend (the tutor) can't finish their homework because they keep playing a video game.
mission: Tell them to turn off the screen.
Give advice on how to focus using 'You should' or 'It's a good idea to'.
start: Tutor: Oh man, I have a lot of homework, but I just can't stop playing this video game! What should I do?

title: Wrap-up
recap: Vocabulary: turn off, focus, video game, notification, screen
Phrases: You should... / You shouldn't... / It's a good idea to...
Skill: Identify things that interrupt studying and give advice on how to avoid them.
final_task: In one sentence, use one of today's phrases to give me advice on how to stay focused when the TV is on.
challenge: Next time you study, turn off the notifications on your screen and see if it helps you focus better.
